messages.message: ### Step 2: Morphosyntactic Requirement Definition Goal: For Japanese, specify per-token morphosyntax needed to realize the Step 1 Interpretation Lock. Requirements (ONE Markdown table): - Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Requirement] - In [Target Requirement], make comparative direction unambiguous and add a 1-line literal back-translation check. Output: ONLY the table; no extra prose.

| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Requirement | |-------------|----------------------|--------------------| | Tant' | Intensifier indicating a high degree of bitterness | Japanese **とても** (adverb) modifying the adjective 苦い; back‑translation check: “so” | | è (1) | Copular verb linking implicit subject “it” to predicate “bitter” | Japanese **だ** (copula) after the adjective phrase; back‑translation check: “is” | | amara | Predicate adjective “bitter” | Japanese **苦い** (i‑adjective) as predicate; back‑translation check: “bitter” | | che (comparative) | Subordinator introducing a comparative clause | Japanese **ほど** (comparative particle) after the adjective phrase; back‑translation check: “that” (as in “as … as”) | | poco | Adverb meaning “little” (small amount) | Japanese **少し** (adverb) modifying the comparative adjective; back‑translation check: “little” | | è (2) | Copular verb linking “death” to comparative predicate | Japanese **は** (topic marker) + **だ** (copula) after “death”; back‑translation check: “is” | | più | Comparative adverb “more” (direction: death > X) | Japanese **より** (comparative particle) indicating “more than”; back‑translation check: “more” | | morte | Noun “death”, the benchmark of bitterness | Japanese **死** (noun) marked with **は** as topic; back‑translation check: “death” | | ma | Coordinating conjunction expressing contrast | Japanese **しかし** (conjunctive adverb) at clause start; back‑translation check: “but” | | per | Preposition indicating purpose (“in order to”) | Japanese **ために** (purpose particle) following the infinitive verb; back‑translation check: “for” | | trattar | Infinitive “to treat/discuss” | Japanese **論じる** (verb) in the **dictionary form** before **ために**; back‑translation check: “treat” | | del | Prepositional phrase “of the” | Japanese **の** (genitive particle) linking noun “good” to preceding verb; back‑translation check: “of the” | | ben | Abstract noun “good” | Japanese **善** (noun) as object of **論じる**; back‑translation check: “good” | | ch'i' | Relative pronoun “that I” | Japanese **私が** (relative clause marker) preceding the verb; back‑translation check: “that I” | | vi | Locative adverb “there” | Japanese **そこ** (demonstrative adverb) as locative complement; back‑translation check: “there” | | trovai | Past historic “found” | Japanese **見つけた** (past tense verb) following **私が**; back‑translation check: “found” | | dirò | Future “I will tell” | Japanese **言うだろう** (future‑like expression) or **言うつもりだ**; back‑translation check: “I will tell” | | de | Preposition “of” introducing discourse domain | Japanese **について** (post‑position) after the noun phrase; back‑translation check: “of” | | l'altre | Determiner + adjective “the other” | Japanese **他の** (adjectival noun) modifying **もの**; back‑translation check: “the other” | | cose | Plural noun “things” | Japanese **もの** (noun) as head of the object phrase; back‑translation check: “things” | | ch'i' (2) | Relative pronoun “that I” (second occurrence) | Japanese **私が** introducing relative clause; back‑translation check: “that I” | | v'ho | Perfect auxiliary “have … there” (locative clitic) | Japanese **そこに** (locative) + **見た** (perfective verb) – no auxiliary needed; back‑translation check: “have … there” | | scorte | Past participle “seen” (agreeing with plural) | Japanese **見た** (past verb) agreeing with **もの**; back‑translation check: “seen” |

### Step 3: Pre-assembled Lexical Inventory Create placeable Japanese components for Step 4. Output ONLY bullet list; ONE LINE per bullet. - Line <ID>: <Phrase 1> / <Phrase 2> / <Phrase 3> Where <ID> is the leading integer at the start of the source line. Hook: each phrase must satisfy the Step 2 Requirements table for that line (including the literal back-translation checks). Rules: Each phrase is directly placeable in the final line (no glue-only fragments). Must keep the line’s main predicate + any required linkage (result/purpose/relative); do not output only a subordinate fragment. Avoid embedding clause-linking connectors inside a phrase; keep phrases as clean, placeable propositions and let Step 4 add any necessary linking function-words/morphology. For comparatives, preserve direction and include comparator/degree in the phrase. No punctuation characters inside phrases; keep phrases short; no newlines.

- Line 7: それはとても苦いです死はそれより少しだけ苦い / それはとても苦いほど死はそれより少しだけ苦い / それはとても苦いです死はそれより僅かに苦い - Line 8: しかし善の論じるために私がそこに見つけた / しかし善のことを論じるために私がそこに見つけた / しかし善の論じることのために私がそこに見つけた - Line 9: 私はそこに見た他のものについて言うだろう / 私がそこに見た他のものについて言うつもりだ / そこに見た他のものについて私は言うだろう

### Step 4: Slot-Based Syntactic Assembly Assemble Step3 components into Japanese lines; keep the same number of lines. Use Step3 Final Form as contiguous substrings; reorder within-line as needed. If simple concatenation is ungrammatical or produces a predicate-clash, you MAY insert only function-words and/or inflectional morphology needed for grammatical joining; do NOT add new content words. When adding linking function-words/morphology, match the relation implied by the source line (result/purpose/relative) and do NOT turn it into a contrast relation unless the source explicitly contrasts. Semantic completeness: each Target Text MUST express the full Locked Meaning for that Source Line; do NOT drop the main predicate when the line contains a main predicate + linked clause. Punctuation: copy ONLY end punctuation from the source line to the END of Target Text; add NO internal punctuation. For each source line output ONLY this block (labels verbatim): Source Line: <copy exact source line> Line Inventory: - <copy the phrases you chose from Step 3 for this line> Assembly Notes: - If you inserted any function-words/morphology for joining, list them briefly. Target Text: <assembled target line> If you forgot a necessary phrase from Step 3: re-insert it (no new content words).

**Source Line:** 7 Tant' è amara che poco è più morte;
**Line Inventory:** - それはとても苦いです死はそれより少しだけ苦い
**Assembly Notes:** - No additional function‑words or morphology were needed; the two clauses are placed consecutively as in the source.
**Target Text:** それはとても苦いです死はそれより少しだけ苦い;
---
**Source Line:** 8 ma per trattar del ben ch'i' vi trovai,
**Line Inventory:** - しかし善の論じるために私がそこに見つけた
**Assembly Notes:** - Inserted the accusative particle **を** after **善** to form the object marker required by the verb **論じる**. Resulting phrase: **しかし善を論じるために私がそこに見つけた**.
**Target Text:** しかし善を論じるために私がそこに見つけた,
---
**Source Line:** 9 dirò de l'altre cose ch'i' v'ho scorte.
**Line Inventory:** - 私はそこに見た他のものについて言うだろう
**Assembly Notes:** - No additional function‑words or morphology were needed; the phrase already contains the future predicate and the relative clause.
**Target Text:** 私はそこに見た他のものについて言うだろう.

### Step 5: Self-Correction via Back-Translation & Grammatical Check Verify each Step4 line vs Reference Translation + Locked Meaning; correct within-line only. Allowed: reorder within the line; re-insert only Step4 Missing; fix function-word/morphology anywhere; never add new content words; never move across lines. Punctuation rule: do NOT introduce new internal punctuation; only keep the end punctuation transferred from the source line. Per line output bullets with EXACT fields: - Line #: <ID> - Target Text (from Step 4): <...> - Back-Translation (literal into the reference translation's language): <...> - Reference Translation (line-aligned): <...> - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct <OK|FAIL>, Coverage <OK|FAIL>, Meaning Drift <OK|FAIL>, Comparative Orientation <OK|FAIL|N/A>, Hallucination <OK|FAIL> - If any FAIL: Corrected Target Text: <...> End Punct: compare last non-whitespace char of Target Text vs Source Line. Line # rule: <ID> is the leading integer at the start of that Source Line. After all lines: if any FAIL, label final as UNVERIFIED and list failing Line # values. Output final Japanese text in ONE code block, line by line.

- Line #: 7 - Target Text (from Step 4): それはとても苦いです死はそれより少しだけ苦い; - Back-Translation (literal): It is very bitter death is a little more bitter than it; - Reference Translation (line‑aligned): So bitter is it that death is little more. - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct **OK**, Coverage **OK**, Meaning Drift **OK**, Comparative Orientation **OK**, Hallucination **OK**
- Line #: 8 - Target Text (from Step 4): しかし善を論じるために私がそこに見つけた, - Back-Translation (literal): But to discuss good I found there, - Reference Translation (line‑aligned): But in order to treat of the good that there I found, - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct **OK**, Coverage **FAIL**, Meaning Drift **FAIL**, Comparative Orientation **N/A**, Hallucination **OK** - Corrected Target Text: しかし私がそこに見つけた善を論じるために,
- Line #: 9 - Target Text (from Step 4): 私はそこに見た他のものについて言うだろう. - Back-Translation (literal): I will say about the other things I saw there. - Reference Translation (line‑aligned): I will tell of the other things that I have seen there. - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct **OK**, Coverage **OK**, Meaning Drift **OK**, Comparative Orientation **N/A**, Hallucination **OK**
**UNVERIFIED** – failing lines: 8
```text それはとても苦いです死はそれより少しだけ苦い; しかし私がそこに見つけた善を論じるために, 私はそこに見た他のものについて言うだろう. ```
